text:
sophia: heads-up — we've got multiple EU customers reporting 800–1200ms tails and intermittent 401s for /v1/generate. Billing team also flagged an unexpected spike from EU orgs. Traces show requests hitting us-west POPs. any ideas?

kevin: can you drop a couple of request ids and a quick repro? i'll run a dig from my laptop to compare.

support-ops: sample reqs: rcv_2026-03-17_aa12, rcv_2026-03-17_bb34 — attached logs show 401 + X-Pop: us-west-2 in response. customers say DNS shows eu endpoint.

netops: i pulled the geoip rollout logs — the new maxmind DB pushed ~2h ago but sync to AMS edge failed on one node. rsync error: 
```
rsync: mkstemp "/var/cache/geoip/GeoIP.mmdb.P6w" failed: No space left on device (28)
```
That node is still returning older routing table which maps some IP blocks -> us-west answers.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0317-73 (severity: high) — paging infra oncall.

maria: mitigation: we can flip the routing fallback to prefer `eu-*` model variants and increase DNS TTL for eu records while i evict the bad cache. temporary header-based workaround for affected customers: `X-Force-Region: eu-central-1` — document this in support reply.

kevin: repro steps i ran from london: 
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 eu.api.redwood.ai A
93.184.216.34  <-- this resolved to us-west edge IP
$ curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{remote_ip}
"
```
Shows the host resolving to US IP and then auth failure (we're seeing auth tokens validated against eu keys, so cross-pop token mismatch causes 401).

support-ops: customer-friendly reply drafted: short explanation + mitigation steps (add X-Force-Region header or point to eu model alias). asked billing-team to hold any auto-invoices tied to the spike until we confirm root cause.

billing-team: acknowledged — we'll freeze auto-billing adjustments for the affected org ids and open a separate billing ticket. preliminary delta: ~3.2k requests rerouted in last 3 hours, estimated $450 in overcharge risk if not corrected.

maria: immediate action plan: 1) cordon AMS edge node, 2) free space and re-push GeoIP DB, 3) force a small DNS prefill to eu edges (TTL 30s), 4) monitor 401/latency key metrics. doing 1–2 now.

sophia: thanks. once you confirm the node is cordoned i'll notify the customers and include repro + temporary header workaround. can someone add the dig + curl snippets to the incident timeline?

netops: cordoned node ams-3 (id: edge-ams-3). freed 2.1GB, rsync resumed and verified checksum. pushed out new db; prefill started.

support-ops: quick verification: ran curl from frankfurt — now resolves to eu edge and returns 200 for same token. 
```
$ curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{remote_ip}
"
```

kevin: nice. i'll keep an eye on latency graphs for the next hour and confirm no further cross-region routing.

maria: leaving the routing fallback policy bumped for 2 hours, then we'll revert. add postmortem to the incident with root cause = disk full causing geoip DB not to update on one edge node, which led to stale routing answers.

sophia: perfect. pls add the customer communications draft to the incident and hand to solutions to send. closing loop here once billing confirms credits. :thumbsup:
